children: Stifel has resumed coverage of IDEAYA Biosciences
at Buy, saying that the company's combination of darovasertib and crizotinib in first-line metastatic uveal melanoma could become the standard of care.
The firm has a price target of $48 (~40% upside based on Oct. 13 close).
Analyst Laura Prendergast said that the combo is set to become the SoC "in HLA-A*02:01-negative mUM with HLA-agnostic label," adding she is modeling a late Q2 2027 approval.
Crizotinib is already approved and marketed by Pfizer
under the name Xalkori for non-small cell lung cancer. Pfizer is partnered with IDEAYA on trials of the darovasertib/crizotinib combo for uveal melanoma.
Prendergrast sees worldwide revenue of ~$1.42B by 2035.

Elsewhere in the pipeline, she highlighted the first-in-class, DLL3-targeting antibody-drug conjugate IDE849, which is in phase 1/2 for small cell lung cancer. The asset is set to move into phase 3 trial for those with extensive stage SCLC whose disease has progressed following treatment with Amgen's
Imdelltra (tarlatamab) by the end of the year.
Prendergrast is projecting global sales of IDE849 of $643M by 2035.

title: IDEAYA resumed at Buy at Stifel on combo treatment for uveal melanoma
